claim: Hedgehog (Hh), Wingless (Wg), and Decapentaplegic (Dpp) are morphogen signaling proteins that disperse across tissues to activate signal transduction in target cells.
source: Morphogen signaling proteins disperse across tissues to activate signal transduction in target cells. We investigated dispersion of Hedgehog (Hh), Wnt homolog Wingless (Wg), and Bone morphogenic protein homolog Decapentaplegic (Dpp) in the Drosophila wing imaginal disc.
evidence: This is stated directly in the abstract and introduction as the subject of investigation.

claim: Less than 5% of Hh is taken up by disc cells and activates signaling.
source: We found that <5% of Hh and <25% of Wg are taken up by disc cells and activate signaling.
evidence: This is a direct quantitative measurement reported in the abstract.

claim: Less than 25% of Wg is taken up by disc cells and activates signaling.
source: We found that <5% of Hh and <25% of Wg are taken up by disc cells and activate signaling.
evidence: This is a direct quantitative measurement reported in the abstract.

claim: The amount of Hh taken up and initiating signaling did not change when Hh expression was varied between 50 and 200%.
source: The amount of morphogen that is taken up and initiates signaling did not change when the level of morphogen expression was varied between 50 and 200% (Hh) or 50 and 350% (Wg).
evidence: This is a direct statement of experimental results in the abstract.

claim: The amount of Wg taken up and initiating signaling did not change when Wg expression was varied between 50 and 350%.
source: The amount of morphogen that is taken up and initiates signaling did not change when the level of morphogen expression was varied between 50 and 200% (Hh) or 50 and 350% (Wg).
evidence: This is a direct statement of experimental results in the abstract.

claim: Similar properties of regulated delivery were observed for Dpp.
source: Similar properties were observed for Dpp.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a finding.

claim: The extent of Hh signaling in the disc was unaffected by the presence or absence of tracheal and myoblast cells.
source: We found that the extent of signaling in the disc was unaffected by the presence or absence of the tracheal and myoblast cells, suggesting that the mechanism that disperses Hh specifies its destinations to particular cells, and that target cells do not take up Hh from a common pool.
evidence: This is a direct statement of experimental results in the abstract.

claim: The mechanism that disperses Hh specifies its destinations to particular cells.
source: We found that the extent of signaling in the disc was unaffected by the presence or absence of the tracheal and myoblast cells, suggesting that the mechanism that disperses Hh specifies its destinations to particular cells, and that target cells do not take up Hh from a common pool.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental results stated in the abstract.

claim: Target cells do not take up Hh from a common pool.
source: We found that the extent of signaling in the disc was unaffected by the presence or absence of the tracheal and myoblast cells, suggesting that the mechanism that disperses Hh specifies its destinations to particular cells, and that target cells do not take up Hh from a common pool.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental results stated in the abstract.

claim: Morphogen signaling proteins control many aspects of development, homeostasis, and disease.
source: Signaling by morphogen proteins controls many aspects of development, homeostasis, and disease (Garcia et al., 2018; Tabata and Takei, 2004; Taipale and Beachy, 2001).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Morphogen proteins distribute across tissues forming concentration gradients that induce signal transduction and activate gene expression in a concentration-dependent manner.
source: These signaling proteins are released from cells that produce them, and they distribute across the tissues they target, forming concentration gradients that induce signal transduction and activate gene expression in a concentration-dependent manner.
evidence: This is a statement of established knowledge in the field.

claim: For more than a century, it was assumed that morphogens spread across tissues by passive diffusion in extracellular space.
source: For more than a century, it was assumed that morphogens spread across tissues by passive diffusion in extracellular space (either 'free' or 'restricted'), and both experimental observations and theoretical modeling have been offered in support (Rogers and Schier, 2011).
evidence: This is a historical statement supported by citation.

claim: Spreading morphogen proteins have been proposed to exist in various forms, including as multimeric complexes or encapsulated in lipoprotein particles, exosomes, or micelles.
source: Spreading morphogen proteins have been proposed to exist in various forms, including as multimeric complexes or encapsulated in lipoprotein particles, exosomes, or micelles (Christian, 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous literature.

claim: Diffusion-based models assume that signaling is proportional to amounts of signaling proteins produced by designated groups of cells.
source: Implicit in these models are the ideas that signaling is proportional to amounts of signaling proteins produced by designated groups of cells, and that release creates an extracellular pool of signaling protein that distributes in extracellular fluid in ways that are dependent on interactions with substances that are encountered or until they are removed from the pool by degradation or by receptor-mediated absorption.
evidence: This is a description of assumptions in diffusion-based models.

claim: Diffusion-based models assume that release of morphogens creates an extracellular pool that distributes in extracellular fluid.
source: Implicit in these models are the ideas that signaling is proportional to amounts of signaling proteins produced by designated groups of cells, and that release creates an extracellular pool of signaling protein that distributes in extracellular fluid in ways that are dependent on interactions with substances that are encountered or until they are removed from the pool by degradation or by receptor-mediated absorption.
evidence: This is a description of assumptions in diffusion-based models.

claim: Diffusion-based models assume that the extracellular pool is formed by constitutive release from producing cells.
source: The pool is assumed to be formed by constitutive release from producing cells.
evidence: This is a description of assumptions in diffusion-based models.

claim: An alternative mechanism of morphogen dispersion is direct exchange at cell-cell contacts.
source: An alternative mechanism of dispersion is direct exchange at cell-cell contacts, and the contrasts with diffusion-based modes of dissemination have been reviewed extensively (Gradilla and Guerrero, 2013; Kornberg, 2017; Kornberg, 2016; Roy and Kornberg, 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citations to review articles.

claim: Cytonemes are specialized filopodia that are conduits for transporting and transferring signaling proteins to target cells at synaptic contacts.
source: Specialized filopodia called cytonemes are conduits that transport and transfer signaling proteins to target cells at synaptic contacts (González-Méndez et al., 2020; González-Méndez et al., 2017; Kornberg, 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Genetic conditions that impair cytonemes reduce cytoneme contacts and compromise signaling.
source: Evidence for the essential role of cytonemes in morphogen signaling includes many identified genetic conditions that impair cytonemes, reduce cytoneme contacts, and compromise signaling.
evidence: This is a summary of evidence from the literature.

claim: Cytonemes contain actin filaments, ribosomes, and proteins that confer voltage sensitivity, calcium dependence, and glutamatergic activity.
source: Although their fine structure is not fully understood, cytonemes contain actin filaments, ribosomes, and proteins that confer voltage sensitivity, calcium dependence, and glutamatergic activity (Huang et al., 2019; Junyent et al., 2020; Wood et al., 2021).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Cytoneme synapses have features characteristic of neuronal glutamatergic synapses, including close apposition of pre- and postsynaptic membranes.
source: These features, as well as the close apposition of pre- and postsynaptic membranes at cytoneme synapses, are also characteristic of neuronal glutamatergic synapses.
evidence: This is a comparison based on cited literature.

claim: Neuronal synapses titrate signaling by frequency and quantity of neurotransmitter release from synaptic vesicles and by efficiency of neurotransmitter clearance from the synaptic gap.
source: Neuronal synapses have another key feature—signaling is titrated by frequency and quantity of neurotransmitter release from synaptic vesicles, and by efficiency of neurotransmitter clearance from the synaptic gap (Blakely and Edwards, 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous literature.

claim: It is not known if cytoneme synapses store morphogen signaling proteins in synaptic vesicles.
source: It is not known if cytoneme synapses also store morphogen signaling proteins in synaptic vesicles and if morphogen signaling at cytoneme synapses is also dependent on regulated release and uptake.
evidence: This is a statement of a knowledge gap.

claim: It is not known if morphogen signaling at cytoneme synapses is dependent on regulated release and uptake.
source: It is not known if cytoneme synapses also store morphogen signaling proteins in synaptic vesicles and if morphogen signaling at cytoneme synapses is also dependent on regulated release and uptake.
evidence: This is a statement of a knowledge gap.

claim: Hh, Wg, and Dpp are evolutionarily conserved morphogen signaling proteins implicated in organogenesis and stem cell maintenance.
source: Hedgehog (Hh), Wnt homolog Wingless (Wg), and Bone morphogenic protein homolog Decapentaplegic (Dpp) are evolutionarily conserved morphogen signaling proteins that have been implicated in organogenesis and stem cell maintenance, and their misregulation in mammals has been linked to inherited diseases and cancers (Briscoe and Thérond, 2013; Morikawa et al., 2016; Nusse and Clevers, 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Misregulation of Hh, Wg, and Dpp in mammals has been linked to inherited diseases and cancers.
source: Hedgehog (Hh), Wnt homolog Wingless (Wg), and Bone morphogenic protein homolog Decapentaplegic (Dpp) are evolutionarily conserved morphogen signaling proteins that have been implicated in organogenesis and stem cell maintenance, and their misregulation in mammals has been linked to inherited diseases and cancers (Briscoe and Thérond, 2013; Morikawa et al., 2016; Nusse and Clevers, 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Hh is expressed specifically and uniformly by posterior (P) compartment cells in the columnar cells of the Drosophila wing imaginal disc.
source: In the columnar cells of the Drosophila wing imaginal disc, Hh is expressed specifically and uniformly by posterior (P) compartment cells (Figure 1A).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 1A.

claim: Hh released by P compartment cells is taken up by anterior (A) compartment cells within 30 μm (10 cells) of the A/P compartment border in the wing blade primordium.
source: In the wing blade primordium of the wing disc, Hh released by P compartment cells is taken up by anterior (A) compartment cells within 30 μm (10 cells) of the anterior/posterior (A/P) compartment border.
evidence: This is a statement of observed spatial distribution.

claim: Transfers of Hh from P to A compartment cells are cytoneme-dependent.
source: Transfers of Hh from the P to A compartment cells are cytoneme-dependent (Bischoff et al., 2013; Chen et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Hh in the A compartment distributes to form a concentration gradient that induces signal transduction and activates expression of target genes in partially overlapping stripes.
source: Hh in the A compartment distributes to form a concentration gradient that induces signal transduction and activates expression of target genes in partially overlapping stripes (Callejo et al., 2011; Chen et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Hh target gene expression domains reflect graded responses to Hh, from highest and 'short-range' (engrailed, patched, and dpp) to lowest and 'long-range' (cubitus interruptus).
source: These domains of expression reflect graded responses to Hh, from highest and 'short-range' (engrailed [en], patched [ptc], and dpp) to lowest and 'long-range' (cubitus interruptus [ci]).
evidence: This is a description of the spatial pattern of gene expression.

claim: The spatial relationships of Hh target gene expression domains are reproducible with single-cell resolution.
source: The spatial relationships of these domains are reproducible, with single-cell resolution.
evidence: This is a statement about the precision of the pattern.

claim: Approximately 5.2% of Hh in normal discs is in the A compartment.
source: Quantification of Hh detected by antibody staining in the entire A and P compartments of the wing primordium of normal discs (2× WT) showed that approximately 5.2% was in the A compartment (n=7; standard deviation [SD]=1.2%).
evidence: This is a direct quantitative measurement.

claim: Hh amounts in the P compartment are proportional to gene dosage in genotypes with 1, 2, 3, or 4 hh genes.
source: As expected, Hh amounts were proportional to gene dosage in the P compartment portion of the rectangular region.
evidence: This is stated as an experimental result.

claim: Hh amounts in the A compartment were not detectably different in genotypes with 1, 2, 3, or 4 hh genes.
source: Analysis of the anterior portion of the rectangular region revealed that Hh amounts were not detectably different in genotypes with 1, 2, 3, or 4 hh genes (Figure 2A,B, Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is stated as an experimental result and shown in figures.

claim: Most Hh produced in the P compartment is not taken up or retained by A compartment cells.
source: In sum, these results are consistent with the idea that most Hh produced in the P compartment is not taken up or retained by A compartment cells, and that Hh uptake is not linked directly to production.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental results.

claim: Hh uptake is not linked directly to production.
source: In sum, these results are consistent with the idea that most Hh produced in the P compartment is not taken up or retained by A compartment cells, and that Hh uptake is not linked directly to production.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental results.

claim: Genotypes with 1, 2, 3, or 4 hh genes had amounts of hh RNA in wing discs which increased with gene dosage and scaled linearly.
source: Genotypes with 1 (1× WT), 2 (2× WT), 3 (2× WT, 1× BAC), or 4 (2× WT, 2× BAC) hh genes had amounts of hh RNA in wing discs which increased with gene dosage and scaled linearly.
evidence: This is a direct statement of qPCR measurement results.

claim: Hh protein in the P compartment increased 2.9× in genotypes with 3 hh genes versus 1.
source: Hh protein in the P compartment (Hh-producing) cells of the wing blade primordium increased 2.9× in genotypes with 3 hh genes versus 1.
evidence: This is a direct quantitative measurement.

claim: Both hh RNA and Hh protein are produced in direct proportion to gene dosage in the range of 1-4 gene copies.
source: These results show that in this range of gene copy number, both hh RNA and Hh protein are produced in direct proportion to gene dosage.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the qPCR and antibody staining data.

claim: The amount of hh RNA in wing discs with hh-Gal4 and UAS-hh:GFP transgenes increased approximately 15× over WT.
source: We also measured hh RNA in wing discs with 2 WT hh genes and transgenes containing hh-Gal4 and UAS-hh:GFP, and observed that the amount increased approximately 15× over WT.
evidence: This is a direct statement of qPCR measurement results.

claim: The size of the Ptc band did not change in discs with 1, 2, 3, or 4 hh gene copies.
source: As shown in Figure 1D,E, the size of the Ptc band did not change in discs with 1, 2, 3, or 4 hh gene copies, despite the differences in hh RNA and Hh protein amounts (Figure 1D,E, Figure 1—figure supplement 1 and 2).
evidence: This is stated as an experimental result and shown in figures.

claim: Hh overexpression driven by hh-Gal4 changed both the size and shape of the Ptc band.
source: In contrast, Hh overexpression driven by hh-Gal4 changed both the size and shape of the Ptc band.
evidence: This is stated as an experimental result.

claim: Expression of Knot did not change in genotypes with 1–4 hh gene copies.
source: Expression of Knot (Kn), which like Ptc expression is regulated by Hh signaling (Vervoort et al., 1999), did not change in genotypes with 1–4 hh gene copies (Figure 1—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is stated as an experimental result and shown in a figure.

claim: Wing dimensions were not dependent on hh gene copy or expression in genotypes with 1-4 hh genes.
source: These wing dimensions were not dependent on hh gene copy or expression (Figure 1F,G).
evidence: This is stated as an experimental result and shown in figures.

claim: Only the hh-Gal4-driven (~15×) overexpression changed wing shape significantly.
source: We monitored wing shape by comparing the length/width ratios of the different genotypes, and determined that only the hh-Gal4-driven (~15×) overexpression changed it significantly (Figure 1G).
evidence: This is stated as an experimental result and shown in a figure.

claim: L3 wing discs were similar in appearance except for the hhGal4 genotype, which had an outgrowth anterior to the wing blade primordium.
source: L3 wing discs were also similar in appearance except for the hhGal4 genotype, which had an outgrowth anterior to the wing blade primordium (Figure 1H).
evidence: This is stated as an experimental observation and shown in a figure.

claim: The processes of production, maturation, secretion, transport, and uptake that disperse Hh in the wing disc generate a distribution in target cells that is insensitive to changes in Hh amounts that 1–4 hh gene copies generate.
source: These findings indicate that the processes of production, maturation, secretion, transport, and uptake that disperses Hh in the wing disc generates a distribution in targets cells that is insensitive to changes in Hh amounts that 1–4 hh gene copies generate.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental results.

claim: The capacity of the process which buffers against changes in amounts of Hh production is limited, as shown by sensitivity to ~15-fold excess Hh.
source: The sensitivity to an excess of ~15-fold normal Hh generated by hh-Gal4 reveals that the capacity of the process which buffers against changes in amounts of Hh production is limited.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental results.

claim: Hh:GFP amounts in the A compartment decreased in proportion to number of hh genes that encode untagged Hh.
source: In contrast, Hh:GFP amounts in the Hh-receiving cells of the A compartment decreased in proportion to number of hh genes that encode untagged Hh.
evidence: This is stated as an experimental result.

claim: The amount of Hh in the A compartment was constant and did not scale with production.
source: We conclude that the amount of Hh in the A compartment was constant and did not scale with production.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental results.

claim: Hh:GFP was diluted by the presence of untagged Hh in the A compartment.
source: This shows that Hh:GFP was diluted by the presence of untagged Hh, a result which is consistent with the amounts of Hh we detected in the A compartment with α-Hh antibody in genotypes with 1, 2, 3, or 4 hh genes (Figure 2A,B).
evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental results shown in figures.

claim: Extracellular staining detected basolateral GFP fluorescence in Hh:GFP expressing cells.
source: The extracellular staining protocol detected basolateral GFP fluorescence (Figure 2—figure supplement 2), consistent with the observations of Callejo et al., 2011 who reported that Hh moves to the basolateral compartment prior to localization to basolateral cytonemes and export (Callejo et al., 2011).
evidence: This is stated as an experimental observation and shown in a figure, with citation to previous work.

claim: Extracellular Hh:GFP staining decreased in both P and A compartments in the presence of untagged Hh.
source: Extracellular staining decreased in both P and A compartments in the presence of untagged Hh (Figure 2F), indicating that Hh exposed on the exterior of P compartment cells is gated.
evidence: This is stated as an experimental result and shown in a figure.

claim: Hh exposed on the exterior of P compartment cells is gated.
source: Extracellular staining decreased in both P and A compartments in the presence of untagged Hh (Figure 2F), indicating that Hh exposed on the exterior of P compartment cells is gated.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental results.

claim: Hh taken up by A compartment cells represents the population of externalized Hh present on the surface of P compartment cells.
source: Although the results suggest that Hh taken up by A compartment cells represents the population of externalized Hh present on the surface of P compartment cells, they do not reveal whether the release of externalized Hh is regulated.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation of the results.

claim: Animals with one WT dpp and one Dpp BAC allele are viable and their wing size is comparable to WT flies.
source: We created a Dpp-encoding BAC transgene (BD) that rescues dpp haploinsufficiency: animals with one WT dpp and one BD (+/dppH46; +/BD) allele are viable and their wing size is comparable to WT flies (Figure 3A,B), indicating that the Dpp BAC is a functional substitute for a WT dpp gene.
evidence: This is stated as an experimental result and shown in figures.

claim: The Dpp BAC is a functional substitute for a WT dpp gene.
source: We created a Dpp-encoding BAC transgene (BD) that rescues dpp haploinsufficiency: animals with one WT dpp and one BD (+/dppH46; +/BD) allele are viable and their wing size is comparable to WT flies (Figure 3A,B), indicating that the Dpp BAC is a functional substitute for a WT dpp gene.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental results.

claim: Dpp prodomain staining in cells that produce Dpp was approximately double in the four copy genotype compared to the two copy genotype.
source: Staining in cells that produce Dpp was approximately double in the four copy genotype compared to the two copy genotype (Figure 3C,D).
evidence: This is stated as an experimental result and shown in figures.

claim: Wing size did not differ between genotypes with two or four dpp genes.
source: We found that wing size did not differ between genotypes with two or four dpp genes (Figure 3A,B).
evidence: This is stated as an experimental result and shown in figures.

claim: The width of the pMAD-staining band was not different in wing discs with two or four dpp gene copies.
source: The width of the pMAD-staining band was not different in wing discs with two or four gene copies (Figure 3E,F), indicating that increased Dpp production does not increase signal transduction.
evidence: This is stated as an experimental result and shown in figures.

claim: Increased Dpp production does not increase signal transduction.
source: The width of the pMAD-staining band was not different in wing discs with two or four gene copies (Figure 3E,F), indicating that increased Dpp production does not increase signal transduction.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental results.

claim: Expression of Spalt did not change in genotypes with two or four dpp gene copies.
source: Similarly, expression of Spalt (Salm), which is regulated by Dpp signaling in the wing disc (de Celis et al., 1996), did not change in genotypes with two or four dpp gene copies (Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is stated as an experimental result and shown in a figure.

claim: Dpp signaling in the wing disc is insensitive to increased levels of Dpp production.
source: In sum, these results show that Dpp signaling in the wing disc is insensitive to increased levels of Dpp production.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental results.

claim: Levels of Dpp:Cherry fluorescence in producing cells did not change with the production of untagged Dpp.
source: Evaluation of the two genotypes showed that levels of Dpp:Cherry fluorescence in producing cells did not change with the production of untagged Dpp (Figure 3H,I), and that levels of Dpp:Cherry fluorescence in non-producing, receiving cells decreased in proportion to the number of genes that encode untagged Dpp (Figure 3I').
evidence: This is stated as an experimental result and shown in figures.

claim: Levels of Dpp:Cherry fluorescence in non-producing, receiving cells decreased in proportion to the number of genes that encode untagged Dpp.
source: Evaluation of the two genotypes showed that levels of Dpp:Cherry fluorescence in producing cells did not change with the production of untagged Dpp (Figure 3H,I), and that levels of Dpp:Cherry fluorescence in non-producing, receiving cells decreased in proportion to the number of genes that encode untagged Dpp (Figure 3I').
evidence: This is stated as an experimental result and shown in figures.

claim: The amount of Dpp:Cherry in target cells decreased as the ratio of tagged:untagged Dpp declined, consistent with the idea that transmission of Dpp to targets is regulated.
source: This finding, that the amount of Dpp:Cherry in target cells decreased as the ratio of tagged:untagged Dpp declined, is consistent with the idea that transmission of Dpp to targets is regulated.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental results.

claim: Wg production is proportional to gene copy number in discs with one and two wg genes.
source: α-Wg antibody staining showed that Wg production is proportional to gene copy number in discs with one and two wg genes, and that the wg-Gal4 driver generated approximately seven times more Wg than a single endogenous gene (Figure 4A,A',B).
evidence: This is stated as an experimental result and shown in figures.

claim: The wg-Gal4 driver generated approximately seven times more Wg than a single endogenous gene.
source: α-Wg antibody staining showed that Wg production is proportional to gene copy number in discs with one and two wg genes, and that the wg-Gal4 driver generated approximately seven times more Wg than a single endogenous gene (Figure 4A,A',B).
evidence: This is stated as an experimental result and shown in figures.

claim: The amount of Wg in the neighboring cells that received Wg was unchanged despite differences in Wg expression between genotypes with 1, 2, and 7 functional gene equivalents.
source: Despite the differences in expression between these genotypes, the amount of Wg in the neighboring cells that received Wg was unchanged (Figure 4A,A',B).
evidence: This is stated as an experimental result and shown in figures.

claim: The fraction of Wg present in the neighboring cells relative to the total produced in the wing blade decreased with increasing functional gene dosage, from approximately 41% (one copy) to 24% (two copies), and 3.5% (seven functional equivalents).
source: The fraction of Wg present in the neighboring cells relative to the total produced in the wing blade decreased with increasing functional gene dosage, from approximately 41% (one copy) to 24% (two copies), and 3.5% (seven functional equivalents).
evidence: This is a direct quantitative statement of experimental results.

claim: The patterns of Sens expression were not detectably different in genotypes with 1, 2, and 7 functional wg gene equivalents.
source: α-Sens antibody detects two narrow, parallel stripes of expression that are immediately adjacent to but do not overlap the Wg-expressing cells (Nolo et al., 2000), and the patterns of Sens expression were not detectably different in these genotypes (Figure 4A",C,C').
evidence: This is stated as an experimental result and shown in figures.

claim: The pattern of Dll expression was not different in genotypes with 1, 2, and 7 functional wg gene equivalents.
source: α-Dll antibody detects a region of expression that overlaps Wg-expressing cells (Zecca et al., 1996), and the pattern of Dll expression also was not different in these genotypes (Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is stated as an experimental result and shown in a figure.

claim: Wg transmission to target cells is regulated.
source: These findings indicate that Wg transmission to target cells is regulated.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental results.

claim: Extracellular Wg of both producing and receiving cells increased with gene dosage and expression.
source: We found that extracellular Wg of both producing and receiving cells increased with gene dosage and expression (Figure 4D).
evidence: This is stated as an experimental result and shown in a figure.

claim: Delivery and release of Wg to receiving cells from the basolateral membrane is rate-limiting.
source: This protocol does not distinguish between protein on either the cell surface or associated with cytonemes, but these results suggest that delivery and release to receiving cells from the basolateral membrane is rate-limiting.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation of the results.

claim: The number of cytonemes correlates positively with signal transduction activity in several different contexts.
source: Previous studies in several different contexts showed that the number of cytonemes correlates positively with signal transduction activity. Whereas cells with low signaling activity have few cytonemes, cells with higher levels of signaling have more (Bischoff et al., 2013; Chen et al., 2017; Du et al., 2018; González-Méndez et al., 2017; Huang et al., 2019; Huang and Kornberg, 2016; Mattes et al., 2018; Roy et al., 2011; Roy et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Overexpression of Ihog increases cytoneme stability and Hh signaling in the wing disc.
source: This correlation also holds for mutant conditions that change cytoneme numbers or signaling: an example is overexpression of Ihog which increases cytoneme stability and Hh signaling in the wing disc (González-Méndez et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citation to a previous study.

claim: In genotypes with 1–4 hh genes, neither ASP morphology nor extent of En expression changed.
source: We found that in genotypes with 1–4 hh genes, neither ASP morphology nor extent of En expression changed (Figure 5A–C).
evidence: This is stated as an experimental result and shown in figures.

claim: Hh overexpression driven by hh-Gal4 reduced the ASP stalk and increased the extent of En expression.
source: In contrast, Hh overexpression driven by hh-Gal4 reduced the stalk and increased the extent of En expression.
evidence: This is stated as an experimental result.

claim: The ASP is insensitive to the different amounts of Hh produced by 1–4 gene copies.
source: These results show that the ASP is insensitive to the different amounts of Hh produced by 1–4 gene copies, and are consistent with the idea that Hh delivery is regulated.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental results.

claim: The capacity of the ASP system to buffer against different levels of Hh expression is limited.
source: The sensitivity to hh-Gal4 driven overexpression indicates that the capacity of the ASP system to buffer against different levels of expression is limited.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental results.

claim: The number of distal tip cytonemes in the ASP did not change in genotypes with 1–4 hh genes.
source: Cytonemes that extend from the distal tip of the ASP take up Hh and contain Ptc (Chen et al., 2017), and in the experimental genotypes with 1–4 hh genes, the number of distal tip cytonemes did not change (Figure 5D,E).
evidence: This is stated as an experimental result and shown in figures.

claim: The number of cytonemes and amount of cytoneme-mediated Hh uptake are insensitive to conditions that reduce or increase Hh production by a factor of 2 relative to WT.
source: We conclude that the number of cytonemes and amount of cytoneme-mediated Hh uptake are insensitive to conditions that reduce or increase Hh production by a factor of 2 relative to WT.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental results.

claim: The extent of En expression in the ASP increased under conditions of Ihog over-expression.
source: The extent of En expression in the ASP increased under conditions of Ihog over-expression (btlGal4 UAS-Ihog), consistent with the idea that stabilized cytonemes increased Hh uptake and signaling (Figure 5F).
evidence: This is stated as an experimental result and shown in a figure.

claim: Ihog over-expression in the ptc domain at the A/P compartment border increased the width of the Ptc band.
source: In the wing disc, Ihog over-expression in the ptc domain at the A/P compartment border (ptcGal4 UAS-Ihog) increased both the width of the Ptc band (compare Figure 1E, Figure 5G) and sensitivity to amount of Hh production.
evidence: This is stated as an experimental result and shown in figures.

claim: Ihog over-expression in the ptc domain increased sensitivity to amount of Hh production.
source: In the wing disc, Ihog over-expression in the ptc domain at the A/P compartment border (ptcGal4 UAS-Ihog) increased both the width of the Ptc band (compare Figure 1E, Figure 5G) and sensitivity to amount of Hh production.
evidence: This is stated as an experimental result.

claim: In genotypes with 1, 2 or 3 hh genes and Ihog overexpression, the width of the Ptc band in discs with two copies increased approximately 35% relative to discs with one.
source: In genotypes with 1, 2 or 3 hh genes, the width of the Ptc band in discs with two copies increased approximately 35% relative to discs with one (ANOVA and Tukey; p<0.05), but no significant difference between discs with two or three copies (Figure 5G).
evidence: This is stated as an experimental result and shown in a figure.

claim: Genetic conditions that increase cytoneme numbers also increase Hh signaling of wing disc cells.
source: These results show both that genetic conditions that increase cytoneme numbers also increase Hh signaling of wing disc cells, and that cells that overexpress Ihog have a limited capacity to respond to increases in Hh.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental results.

claim: Cells that overexpress Ihog have a limited capacity to respond to increases in Hh.
source: These results show both that genetic conditions that increase cytoneme numbers also increase Hh signaling of wing disc cells, and that cells that overexpress Ihog have a limited capacity to respond to increases in Hh.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental results.

claim: No change in shf mRNA was detected in genotypes with one and four hh genes.
source: We quantified shf expression in discs with one and four hh genes by quantifying shf transcripts with qPCR; no change in shf mRNA was detected in these genotypes (Figure 6A,B).
evidence: This is stated as an experimental result and shown in figures.

claim: Shf does not control Hh release.
source: This insensitivity to the tested changes in Hh amounts suggests that Shf does not control Hh release.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental results.

claim: qPCR analysis detected no changes to expression of brk, pent, sog, or cv-2 in genotypes with two or four dpp genes.
source: qPCR analysis detected no changes to expression of brk, pent, sog, or cv-2 in genotypes with two or four dpp genes (Figure 6B).
evidence: This is stated as an experimental result and shown in a figure.

claim: Notum expression is not influenced by changes to Wg gene number.
source: Notum expression is induced by Wg signaling and encodes an extracellular deacylase of Wg that inhibits Wg signaling (Minami et al., 1999), but its expression is not influenced by changes to Wg gene number (Figure 6B).
evidence: This is stated as an experimental result and shown in a figure.

claim: Expression of known modulators of the Hh, Dpp, and Wg pathways do not compensate for changes in amounts of morphogen production.
source: In sum, these data do not support the idea that expression of known modulators of the Hh, Dpp, and Wg pathways compensate for changes in amounts of morphogen production, and are consistent with the idea that release is regulated.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental results.

claim: All the ASP, myoblast, and disc cells that are within approximately 60 μm of the Hh-expressing, P compartment disc cells activate Hh signaling.
source: All the ASP, myoblast, and disc cells that are within approximately 60 μm of the Hh-expressing, P compartment disc cells activate Hh signaling (Hatori and Kornberg, 2020).
evidence: This is supported by citation to a previous study.

claim: The primary determinant of Hh signaling in the microenvironment appears to be distance from producing cells.
source: Thus, despite the cell cycle, shape, constitution, and fate differences between the cells in this microenvironment, the primary determinant of Hh signaling appears to be distance from producing cells.
evidence: This is an interpretation based on the observation that cells within a certain distance activate signaling.

claim: Genetic conditions that reduced the number of cells in the target field did not increase the number of remaining cells in the microenvironment that activated Hh signaling.
source: It does not, genetic conditions that reduced the number of cells in the target field did not increase the number of remaining cells in the microenvironment that activated Hh signaling (Figure 8).
evidence: This is stated as an experimental result and shown in a figure.

claim: In the microenvironment, Hh uptake is not determined by production levels, cell type, or number of other cells that also take up Hh.
source: This result shows that in the microenvironment, Hh uptake is not determined by either production levels, cell type, or number of other cells that also take up Hh.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental results.

claim: The finding that Hh uptake is independent of other cells in the target field is not consistent with the idea that Hh populates a shared extracellular pool from which different cells draw.
source: This finding is not consistent with the idea that Hh populates a shared extracellular pool from which different cells draw, a central tenet of diffusion models.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental results in the context of diffusion models.

claim: Dissemination of Hh involves direct cell-to-cell exchanges between one producing and one receiving cell.
source: Our interpretation is that this finding is consistent with cytoneme-mediated signaling and the idea that dissemination of Hh involves direct cell-to-cell exchanges between one producing and one receiving cell.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental results.

claim: Cell-to-cell exchanges of Hh are regulated and are insensitive to modest increases or decreases in Hh production.
source: Our results suggest that these cell-to-cell exchanges are regulated and are insensitive to modest increases or decreases in Hh production.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental results.

claim: The ~20× excess in Hh production relative to amounts transferred to target cells may buffer the system and ensure that Hh is not limiting for the process that regulates its transfer.
source: The ~20× excess in production relative to amounts transferred to target cells may buffer the system and ensure that Hh is not limiting for the process that regulates its transfer.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation of the results.

claim: Cell-to-cell exchanges of Hh are insensitive to increases or decreases in the number of other cells in the target field because they are restricted to interactions between single pairs of cells.
source: And because the exchanges are restricted to interactions between single pairs of cells, they are insensitive to increases or decreases in the number of other cells in the target field.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation of the results.

claim: The idea that morphogen gradients form by diffusion originated before morphogens were discovered to be signaling proteins.
source: The idea that morphogen gradients form by diffusion originated before morphogens were discovered to be signaling proteins, and the first attempt to model gradient formation based on chemical and physical principles assumed that they were small organic molecules that diffuse freely into and out of cells (Crick, 1970).
evidence: This is a historical statement supported by citation.

claim: Diffusion-based dissemination of morphogens is still without direct evidence.
source: Protein moving in an extracellular environment prior to receptor-mediated uptake has been modeled with more complex mathematics (Lander, 2007; Madamanchi et al., 2021), but diffusion-based dissemination is still without direct evidence.
evidence: This is a statement about the state of evidence in the field.

claim: Studies of morphogen proteins that have been interpreted as supporting diffusion-based dissemination have used methods that do not distinguish cell-free protein from cell-bound protein.
source: Studies of morphogen proteins expressed at physiological levels and in normal conditions that have been interpreted as supporting diffusion-based dissemination have used methods that do not distinguish cell-free protein from cell-bound protein.
evidence: This is a critique of previous studies.

claim: Studies interpreted as supporting diffusion have not been carried out in conditions in which cytonemes could be imaged.
source: In addition, these studies have not been carried out in conditions in which cytonemes could be imaged (Stapornwongkul and Vincent, 2021).
evidence: This is a critique of previous studies supported by citation.

claim: It has yet to be established whether effects of defective heparan sulfate proteoglycans on morphogen distribution were due to inhibition of protein movement in extracellular space or to inhibition of cytoneme function.
source: Mutants with defective heparan sulfate proteoglycans that do not distribute morphogens normally are examples, but it has yet to be established whether the observed effects were due to inhibition of protein movement in extracellular space (Bishop et al., 2007; Häcker et al., 2005; McGough et al., 2020; Mii and Takada, 2020) or to inhibition of cytoneme function (Bischoff et al., 2013; González-Méndez et al., 2017).
evidence: This is a statement about ambiguity in interpretation of previous studies, supported by citations.

claim: Protein released from beads, pipets, or overexpressing cells may not disperse by normal routes.
source: However, the protein in these experiments may not disperse by normal routes. In our experiments, Hh release was not gated if Hh was produced at excessively high levels by cells that were genetically engineered for overexpression, in contrast to Hh protein produced at close to normal levels (Figure 1). We suggest that protein released from beads, pipets, or overexpressing cells may not reflect the normal state.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation of the results in the context of previous studies.

claim: Evidence for cytoneme-mediated transfer of signaling proteins at cell-cell contacts is both genetic and histologic.
source: Evidence for cytoneme-mediated transfer of signaling proteins at cell-cell contacts is both genetic and histologic.
evidence: This is a summary statement about the nature of evidence.

claim: Cytonemes defective for proteins that provide essential functions to neuronal synapses do not make normal numbers of functional synaptic contacts, do not disseminate signaling proteins, and are signaling deficient.
source: Cytonemes defective for proteins that provide essential functions to neuronal synapses such as the cell adhesion protein Capricious, the calcium-binding protein Synaptotagmin-4, and potassium rectifying channel Irk-2 do not make normal numbers of functional synaptic contacts, do not disseminate signaling proteins, and are signaling deficient (Huang et al., 2019; Roy et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Hh, Dpp, and Bnl/FGF are visible moving along cytonemes that extend from producing cells and link with receiving cells.
source: Hh, Dpp, and Bnl/FGF are visible moving along cytonemes that extend from producing cells and link with receiving cells, and are also visible after uptake colocalized with their respective receptors in cytonemes that extend from receiving cells and link to producing cells (Capdevila and Guerrero, 1994; Du et al., 2018; Huang et al., 2019; Roy et al., 2014; Torroja et al., 2004).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: The evidence for cytoneme-based dissemination is direct and strong.
source: Thus, the evidence for cytoneme-based dissemination is direct and strong.
evidence: This is a summary statement about the strength of evidence.

claim: The process that distributes signaling proteins into concentration gradients appears to have several components, including regulation of the number of cytonemes that link producing and receiving cells.
source: The process that distributes signaling proteins into concentration gradients that decline with increasing distance from source cells appears to have several components. One regulates the number of cytonemes that link producing and receiving cells.
evidence: This is a summary of findings from the literature.

claim: In the wing disc and ASP systems, the number of cytonemes linking producing and receiving cells correlates with signaling strength.
source: In the wing disc and ASP systems, the number of cytonemes linking producing and receiving cells correlates with signaling strength—cells far from signal sources and low signaling have fewer cytonemes than do cells close to signal sources and high signaling (Du et al., 2018; Roy et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: For Branchless/FGF signaling in the ASP, positive feedback increases the number of relatively short cytonemes of cells with high signaling levels, and negative feedback decreases the number of relatively long cytonemes in cells with lower signaling levels.
source: For Branchless/FGF signaling in the ASP, positive feedback that increases the number of relatively short cytonemes of cells that have high signaling levels and are close to source cells, and negative feedback that decreases the number of relatively long cytonemes in cells that have lower signaling levels and are farther from source cells.
evidence: This is a description of a regulatory mechanism.

claim: The system of feedback regulation contributes to the formation of a spatial gradient of cytoneme number and concentration gradient of Branchless/FGF.
source: This system of regulation contributes to the formation of a spatial gradient of cytoneme number and concentration gradient of Branchless/FGF (Du et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citation to a previous study.

claim: Similar feedback systems may sculpt the cytoneme gradients that disperse Hh and Dpp.
source: Similar feedback systems may sculpt the cytoneme gradients that disperse Hh and Dpp.
evidence: This is a speculative extrapolation from the Branchless/FGF system.

claim: Hh signaling enhances expression of Ptc, a receptor that binds and sequesters Hh, thereby reducing Hh dispersion and shaping the contour and extent of the Hh gradient.
source: Another regulatory mechanism involves feedback responses to signaling. Hh signaling, for example, enhances expression of Ptc, a receptor that binds and sequesters Hh, thereby reducing Hh dispersion and shaping the contour and extent of the Hh gradient (Chen and Struhl, 1996; Li et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: A third regulatory mechanism is the gating which releases constant amounts of Hh, Dpp, and Wg independently of levels of production.
source: A third regulatory mechanism is reported here—the gating which releases constant amounts of Hh, Dpp, and Wg independently of levels of production.
evidence: This is a summary of the main finding of the study.

claim: The amount of Hh detected at the basal surface of producing cells was constant and independent of level of production, suggesting that placement at the basal membrane is gated.
source: We found that the amount of Hh detected at the basal surface of producing cells was constant and independent of level of production, suggesting that placement at the basal membrane is gated.
evidence: This is stated as an experimental observation and interpretation.

claim: Levels of extracellular Hh were less than total Hh in producing cells.
source: This idea is consistent with the observation that levels of extracellular Hh were less than total Hh in these cells, but the possibilities remain that release from producing cells and/or uptake by receiving cells may also be regulated.
evidence: This is stated as an experimental observation.

claim: Release from producing cells and/or uptake by receiving cells may also be regulated.
source: This idea is consistent with the observation that levels of extracellular Hh were less than total Hh in these cells, but the possibilities remain that release from producing cells and/or uptake by receiving cells may also be regulated.
evidence: This is a speculative statement about possible mechanisms.

claim: Investigations of cytoneme biology have been guided by known features of neurons and neuronal signaling.
source: Our investigations of cytoneme biology have been guided by known features of neurons and neuronal signaling, and we have identified many features of cytoneme-mediated signaling that are analogous.
evidence: This is a statement about the research approach.

claim: Many features of cytoneme-mediated signaling are analogous to neuronal signaling, including spatially-specific signaling at synapses, synaptic localization of specific proteins, essential roles for glutamate receptor and transporter, and trans-synaptic calcium transients.
source: These include spatially-specific signaling at synapses that link cells at distances of <40 nm (Roy et al., 2014), synaptic localization of proteins such as the voltage-gated calcium channel and Synaptotagmin, essential roles for the glutamate receptor and glutamate transporter, and trans-synaptic stimulation of calcium transients (Huang et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Calcium-dependent release of glutamate is essential for both cytoneme-mediated signaling and for glutamatergic excitatory neuronal synapses.
source: And calcium-dependent release of glutamate is essential for both cytoneme-mediated signaling and for glutamatergic excitatory neuronal synapses.
evidence: This is a statement about a shared feature.

claim: It remains to be determined how morphogen proteins are released from producing cells and are exposed to receiving cells.
source: It remains for further investigations to determine how morphogen proteins are released from producing cells and are exposed to receiving cells, and if protein transfers at cytoneme synapses are controlled.
evidence: This is a statement about future research directions.

claim: It remains to be determined if protein transfers at cytoneme synapses are controlled.
source: It remains for further investigations to determine how morphogen proteins are released from producing cells and are exposed to receiving cells, and if protein transfers at cytoneme synapses are controlled.
evidence: This is a statement about future research directions.

claim: Delivery of Hh, Dpp, and Wg to target cells is regulated and is not dependent on the amount of protein produced or on constitutive release.
source: The work reported here demonstrates that delivery of Hh, Dpp, and Wg to target cells is regulated and is not dependent on the amount of protein produced or on constitutive release—that differences in production as much as 4× for Hh, 2× for Dpp, and 7× for Wg did not change the amount of uptake or signal transduction.
evidence: This is a summary of the main findings of the study.

claim: Delivery of Hh to a tissue is not influenced by the complexity or size of the target fields.
source: This work also reports that delivery of Hh to a tissue is not influenced by the complexity or size of the target fields—that the presence or absence of Hh-receiving tracheal cells and myoblasts was of no consequence to Hh signaling in the same region of the wing disc.
evidence: This is a summary of the main findings of the study.

claim: The contours of Hh, Dpp, and Wg distributions are determined by controlled exchanges between producing and receiving cells, not by constitutive release from producing cells.
source: The conclusion we draw is that the contours of Hh, Dpp, and Wg distributions are determined by controlled exchanges between producing and receiving cells, not by constitutive release from producing cells.
evidence: This is the main conclusion of the study.

claim: Regulated delivery is an important, defining feature of the process that disperses Hh, Dpp, and Wg across tissues.
source: This is an important, defining feature of the process that disperses these proteins across tissues.
evidence: This is a statement about the significance of the findings.
